paper.title_en: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
paper.abstract_en: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cosα)$, where $α$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cosα)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2α>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2α<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.
